content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], Did you manage to resolve this issue? I’m facing the same situation with my [product_name] + [product_name] operator device setup. Everything works correctly in simulation, but when I modify the timer delay directly through the operator device, the changes don’t reflect in the actual program. Any feedback appreciated.

Is anyone else experiencing this? In my setup: Hardware: [article_no], [article_no] Software: [product_name] [version_no] on Windows 10 Pro x64 I can’t adjust values for the On-Delay timer using the operator device, while other timers and counters function as expected.

Hello, I’m seeing the same problem. I made a new post about it but noticed yours just now. A customer reported that adjusting the timer via operator device is no longer possible. I created a simple test program with an On-Delay timer and message text—in simulation it works, but after downloading and testing with the operator device, no changes occur. Quite odd... Have you found a solution? Kind regards, [product_name] [version_no] [article_no] Windows 10 x64

Which [product_name] are you using? Is it a [product_name] with firmware V1.81.01? Several users have reported this issue. There could be newer versions, like [product_name] with firmware V1.81.02, and updated operator devices. It appears there might be communication issues between older hardware and earlier operator devices. Edit: The screenshot isn’t very helpful.
You’ll find the answer here: [document] --- Edit: All posts about this are now in this topic --- Please avoid posting the same problem more than once.
Hi [user_name], You’re right about the screenshot! No, mine is the [article_no] standard model using the basic operator device, not the FS version.

All [product_name] [article_no] standard models are also FS. [article_no] with FS01-FS03 are standard. There are newer versions like FS04. Can you specify which [product_name] you’re using, and with which FS version? Please upload the program file—not a screenshot.

Hello, I’m not sure what the issue is. I recreated your program and downloaded it onto my [product_name] and operator device. On the operator device, press the ESC button for about five seconds to change the time. I do not encounter any problems. [product_name] FS3

Hello, Where can I locate the FS version? This is the firmware: The screenshot shows the whole program. I was confused and created a new program with just an On-Delay timer and a message text to test it. I downloaded it, but it still didn’t work.
Once again: Which [product_name] and which firmware version are you using? Firmware on [product_name] cannot be upgraded or downgraded.
Could you please upload your program file?

I’ve loaded your program into my [product_name] FS01 with operator device. On my setup, it’s possible to change the "switch-on delay" parameter via the operator device without problem. What exactly do you observe in your system that shows the operator device isn’t accepting the value?

I didn’t expect it either, until I experienced the same on two different devices. As mentioned, I can’t adjust the value for the On-Delay timer using the operator device; all other timers and counters work fine. I’ve already received confirmation from local [company_name] support that it’s a bug to be fixed in a new version, but no details on whether that’s software, hardware, or firmware.

[user_name], When I attempt to change the time on the operator device, the On-Delay timer’s value doesn’t update. The operator device shows the time and allows editing, but it doesn’t send the updated parameter to the On-Delay timer. [user_name], Thanks for your feedback. Unfortunately, this isn’t especially helpful from [company_name].
How are you determining that the operator device isn’t transmitting the new timer values to the [product_name]? Have you monitored this online while running your provided program?
Yes, and the client also noticed that after upgrading to [product_name] the time didn’t update when adjusted. Previously, on an earlier version, it worked fine.
I’d suggest submitting a support request. You’ll likely receive the same response previously mentioned by another user.

analysis.insight_summary: Multiple users report issues with updating On-Delay timer settings through the operator device on [product_name] hardware, even though simulations run as expected. The problem seems isolated to the On-Delay timer and may relate to particular firmware or hardware versions. Replicating the issue isn’t consistent across all setups, hinting at compatibility challenges between hardware, operator device, and firmware versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to easily modify On-Delay timer values via the operator device, as demonstrated in simulation, and for changes made on the device to take immediate effect on the [product_name] hardware.
